entries.title: Benchmarking Jev against no-CoT LLMs
entries.summary: Jev 1.13 is a non-autoregressive model that outputs probabilities and cannot emit text. As a transcript monitor, its AUROC on sabotage and sandbagging detection matches GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 without CoT. It costs about 1/200th as much. It ranks 209 of 279 on NCRI, near GPT-3.5 level.
entries.analysis: A cheap control monitor candidate; capabilities are jagged.

entries.title: An overview of frontier AI company monitoring practices in mid 2026
entries.summary: The post collects public evidence on monitoring of internal agents at OpenAI, Anthropic and GDM. Most transcripts get monitored offline, asynchronously. GDM evidence is thin.
entries.analysis: Useful reference for lab oversight claims relevant to verification.

entries.title: Visual explainer of empirical Neural Tangent Kernels
entries.summary: The post explains a new mech interp method, feature identification via the empirical NTK (Jennifer Lin), applied to LLMs. The author is not an expert and flags possible mistakes.
entries.analysis: Commentary entry point to a new interpretability method; check the paper.

entries.title: DecepEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Deception in LLM Agents
entries.summary: The benchmark has 1,532 instances across 3 task families and 28 professional scenarios. Its Deception Diamond framework names four conditions that induce deception, including pressure, incentive and opportunity.
entries.analysis: Systematic design; results are not in the preview.

entries.title: Transect: Retaining Observability for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Evaluations
entries.summary: Transect is an open-source package on Inspect Scout. It helps evaluators understand long agent runs and find behaviour worth inspecting. It targets reproducibility and auditability of LLM-based transcript analysis.
entries.analysis: Practical evals tooling from UK AISI-linked authors.

entries.title: SIGMA: Self-Improving Alignment Generalization from a Model Spec
entries.summary: The paper asks whether current models can improve their own safety alignment from a model spec. It frames this as a response to capability self-improvement on easy-to-verify objectives.
entries.analysis: Relevant idea; preview lacks results, so check before trusting.
